title: The Four Seasons: Spring, Concerto in E major
hook: Birdsong, a thunderstorm, a sleeping goatherd and a country dance, all in ten minutes.

painting.title: Fêtes vénitiennes
painting.pairingNote: Painted in the same years as the concerto, it shows a couple dancing in a garden while a musician on the right plays the musette, the small bagpipe that Vivaldi imitates in his last movement.

facts: *Spring* is the first of the four concertos known as *The Four Seasons*. Vivaldi probably wrote them between about 1718 and 1723, partly while he was music director at the court of Mantua, and published them in Amsterdam in 1725 as the first four of the twelve concertos in his Op. 8, *Il cimento dell’armonia e dell’inventione* (“The contest between harmony and invention”).

Each concerto came with a sonnet, possibly written by Vivaldi himself. The spring sonnet has three parts, one for each movement: birds, streams and a storm; a goatherd asleep in a meadow; nymphs and shepherds dancing to a bagpipe. Vivaldi printed the lines in the score next to the music that paints them, and even marked the parts (“the barking dog”).

It is a concerto in the Baroque way: a refrain for the whole string band, the [[ritornello|ritornello]], keeps coming back, and between its returns the solo violin paints the scenes of the poem. A harpsichord and bass instruments, the [[continuo|continuo]], hold everything together from underneath.
Instrumental music that tells a story was rare in 1725. *The Four Seasons* is one of the earliest and most detailed examples of what was later called [[programme-music|programme music]].
bigPicture.inOneLine: birds, a stream and a storm (I), a goatherd asleep in the heat (II), a country dance to the bagpipe (III).

movements.heading: Allegro
movements.summary: “Spring has arrived.” A bright, dancing refrain for all the strings opens the movement and returns between the scenes of the sonnet: birdsong, murmuring streams, a short thunderstorm, and the birds again once the storm has passed.

mainIdeas.name: The refrain
mainIdeas.description: a cheerful tune for all the strings, each phrase played loud and then echoed softly.

mainIdeas.name: The birds
mainIdeas.description: the solo violin and two other violins, very high, with trills and chirping repeated notes.

mainIdeas.name: The storm
mainIdeas.description: fast repeated notes in the whole band (thunder) and quick rushing runs from the soloist (lightning).

stops.hear: The whole string band plays a bright, skipping tune; each short phrase is repeated quietly, like an echo
The band falls away; the solo violin and two other violins chirp and trill high up, answering each other
stops.happening: The birds greet the spring with song

stops.hear: The violins play soft, flowing runs of short notes, close together, like water
stops.happening: “The streams flow with a sweet murmur”

stops.hear: The whole band hammers fast repeated notes; the soloist answers with rapid runs shooting upwards
stops.happening: Thunder and lightning. The music turns towards a minor key

stops.hear: The refrain, now darker, in a minor key
The high trills come back in the solo violin
The refrain one last time, ending softly

notice: Listen for the echo in the refrain: loud, then soft, then loud again. It is the same idea as the call and answer of the birds.
In the storm, the thunder is the band and the lightning is the soloist. Try to hear the two layers separately.

movements.heading: Largo e pianissimo sempre
movements.summary: A short, still scene in C-sharp minor: a goatherd asleep in a flowery meadow, his dog beside him. Three layers sound at once, each with a meaning: the violins are the rustling leaves, the solo violin is the sleeper’s long, calm song, and the violas are the dog.

mainIdeas.name: The leaves
mainIdeas.description: the violins play a soft, rocking pattern of two short notes, over and over.

mainIdeas.name: The sleeper
mainIdeas.description: a long, slow melody in the solo violin, floating above the leaves.

mainIdeas.name: The dog
mainIdeas.description: the violas repeat one loud, rough note on every beat. Vivaldi labelled the part “the barking dog” and asked for it loud.

stops.hear: Very quiet rocking notes in the violins; underneath, one note repeated firmly on every beat
stops.happening: The leaves rustle; the viola “dog” starts barking. Vivaldi wrote no bass part for this movement

stops.hear: The solo violin enters with a slow, long-breathed melody
The melody climbs higher and moves to a brighter key for a moment

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The solo line sinks back to where it began; the dog keeps barking to the last bar
stops.happening: The scene stays exactly as it was

notice: The bass is missing. Vivaldi left the cellos and basses out of this movement, so the music seems to float, which suits a scene of sleep.
The “dog” is loud while everything else is marked very soft. Vivaldi wanted the contrast.

movements.heading: Danza pastorale. Allegro
movements.summary: A country dance in a lilting rhythm of three-note groups. Under the tune, the lower strings hold long notes like the [[drone|drone]] of a bagpipe, and the solo violin leads the nymphs and shepherds through several rounds of the dance.

mainIdeas.name: The dance
mainIdeas.description: a swinging tune in the violins, in a long-short rhythm.

mainIdeas.name: The bagpipe
mainIdeas.description: low held notes in the violas and bass, which barely move.

mainIdeas.name: The solo violin’s turns
mainIdeas.description: brighter, more decorated passages between the returns of the dance.

stops.hear: A swinging dance tune over low, held notes that hardly change
The solo violin steps forward with its own, more decorated line
stops.happening: The first solo episode: the dancers start

stops.hear: The dance tune again, the whole band
The solo violin again, with wider leaps and quicker notes
The dance turns darker: the same rhythm in a minor key
stops.happening: A minor-key round of the dance, a brief cloud

stops.hear: The soloist runs up and down in fast notes; the drone continues below
stops.happening: The last and most brilliant episode

stops.hear: The dance tune, back in the bright home key

notice: Listen to the bass line rather than the tune. For long stretches it stays on the same notes, the way a bagpipe’s drone pipes do.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Simon Standage and The English Concert play on period instruments, built or set up as in Vivaldi’s time. Trevor Pinnock directs from the harpsichord, which plays chords under the band as part of the [[continuo|continuo]].

threads.title: The sonnet
threads.body: Every scene in the music follows a line of the poem, in order: the birds, the streams, the storm, the birds again, the sleeper and his dog, the dance.

threads.title: Refrain and episodes
threads.body: In both fast movements a returning refrain frames the scenes. The slow movement has no refrain at all, only one still picture.

threads.title: Who plays what
threads.body: Vivaldi turns the parts of the string band into characters: two violins become birds, the violas become a dog, the basses become a bagpipe.
